Governor Michele Bullock remains focused on combating entrenched inflation.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Three of nine Reserve Bank board members voted against a recent interest rate increase. They argued for waiting to assess the impact of previous hikes on households, expressing concern that the economy could face a sharper downturn and higher unemployment. Conversely, Governor Michele Bullock prioritised addressing persistent inflation, warning that businesses are beginning to accept higher price rises as normal.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The split highlights the tension between managing inflation and avoiding a recession. While some board members fear the central bank might push the economy too far, the governor remains concerned that an entrenched inflationary mindset will be difficult to reverse without further rate hikes.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.text: Rio Tinto has agreed to provide US$250m to help clean up the Panguna mine in Bougainville. The site was abandoned in 1989 after violent protests and a civil war caused by environmental destruction and profit disputes. The company will now contribute to remediation efforts following a consultation process.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The mine caused significant environmental damage, leaving polluted rivers and unstable rubble. Local leaders view the fund as a foundation for addressing these issues and improving access to clean water and infrastructure. The site is also central to Bougainville's economic hopes for future independence.
